Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains. Continue reading...

kenya.title: Njeri Mwangi
kenya.summary: Njeri Mwangi Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:18 pm Being the wife of a well-known activist is not for the faint-hearted, but for Njeri Mwangi, it is a way of life and a role that she has played since her husband, Boniface Mwangi, jumped into the world of activism.   In 2025, Mwangi’s resolve was tested as she had to endure the kidnapping and detention of her husband in Tanzania under mysterious circumstances.   Clips shared by human rights activists online, Mwangi could be seen distraught as she pleaded for her husband’s release from an undisclosed location in Tanzania.   The mother of three called upon the governments of Tanzania and Kenya to secure her husband’s release and also participated in protests held in Kenya demanding her husband’s release.   Aside from her activism efforts, Mwangi, through her work as the co-founder of PAWA 254,  left an impact on the youth, guiding new programmes and dialogues in 2025 that blended art, culture, and civic education.   Njeri is an accomplished journalist, having produced powerful investigative documentaries for the BBC, including "Forced to Beg: Tanzania's Trafficked Kids" and "The Baby Stealers".   Her efforts as an activist have seen her face death threats and periods of exile, demonstrating a fierce resilience and unwavering commitment to her cause.    Her BBC documentaries have received significant industry recognition, including an Emmy nomination and nominations for the Amadi Prize and the Rory Peck Award for prestigious journalism.   The Association for Women's Rights in Development selected her as one of 15 “fierce feminist journalists” changing the world, explicitly calling her a “frontline activist” in human rights and anti-corruption efforts.

kenya.title: Njeri Wa Migwi
kenya.summary: Njeri Wa Migwi Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:15 pm Njeri W a Migwi is a fearless Kenyan human rights defender and a formidable voice in the fight against gender-based violence (GBV), transforming her personal experience of a decade of domestic abuse into a powerful national movement.   As the Co-Founder and Executive Director of Usikimye , she has established a network of safe houses that provide vital refuge, medical aid, and legal support for survivors, including women, children, and members of the LGBTQ community. Her activism extends beyond shelters; in January 2024, she was a leading organiser of nationwide anti-femicide protests in Kenya, drawing critical attention to the silent pandemic of violence against women.   Her unwavering commitment and impact have been acknowledged through several significant accolades, particularly in 2025.   In November 2025, she was the recipient of the Positive Impact Influencer of the Year award at the Pulse Influencer Awards.   This adds to her previous honours, which include being named the CEO of the Year at the 2024 East Africa Women of Excellence Awards and the Human Rights Defender of the Year in 2021 by the Defenders Coalition.

kenya.title: Emmanuel Wanyonyi
kenya.summary: Emmanuel Wanyonyi Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:11 pm At just 21 years old, Emmanuel Wanyonyi is already a World and Olympic champion and has put himself on course to be one of, if not the best, athletes in the 800m.   Wanyonyi was crowned the 800m world champion after a strong final kick pushed him to victory in the World Athletics Championship in Tokyo, Japan, in September 2025.   The young runner burst onto the scene in 2024, but despite his fast rise, he has maintained professionalism and clean competition, representing Kenya with honour and pride.   Aside from his exploits in the Tokyo championships, Wanyonyi also recorded wins in the Monaco Diamond League in July and the London Athletics Meet in September, setting a world-leading time and meet record, respectively.   He has demonstrated his abilities in the 1500m and Road Mile, winning both competitions in the Kingston Slam competition in Jamaica back in April.   His extraordinary form throughout the year culminated in the prestigious recognition of being crowned the 2025 World Athletics Male Track Athlete of the Year in December, a testament to his rapid ascent and dominance in his discipline.   Beyond the track, Wanyonyi has been a source of inspiration to young people from rural areas. He often encourages discipline, hard work, and focus, using his journey as proof that success comes through persistence.

kenya.title: Beatrice Chebet
kenya.summary: Beatrice Chebet Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:07 pm Beatrice Chebet is a phenomenal long-distance runner, affectionately nicknamed the "Smiling Assassin" for her calm demeanour before unleashing a devastating finishing kick on the track.   Hailing from Kericho, a region renowned for producing elite athletes, she has etched her name in the annals of athletics history as the first woman to simultaneously hold both Olympic and World Championship titles and world records in the 5,000 metres and 10,000 metres events.   A Major in the Kenyan Police Service, Chebet's journey from a promising junior athlete to a global superstar is a testament to her dedication, versatility across track and cross country, and relentless pursuit of excellence.   The year 2025 has been nothing short of historic for Chebet, who added the only missing accolades to her illustrious career: World Championship gold medals.   At the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo in September, she achieved a stunning distance double, winning gold in both the 10,000 metres (Kenya's first gold in the event since 2015) and the 5,000 metres with a final-lap sprint that left her competitors, including compatriot Faith Kipyegon, behind.   Her record-breaking form continued from earlier in the season when, in July 2025 at the Prefontaine Classic in Eugene, she became the first woman in history to break the 14-minute barrier in the 5,000m, setting a new world record of 13:58.06.   These monumental achievements have seen her voted Kenya's Female Long-Distance Athlete of the Year for 2025 and put her in a league of her own, standing alongside legends like Usain Bolt and Kenenisa Bekele as an athlete who has dominated multiple distances with world titles and records.

kenya.title: Rose Njeri Tunguru
kenya.summary: Rose Njeri Tunguru Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:05 pm Before 2025, the name Rose Njeri Tunguru was not familiar to most Kenyans, but a simple website propelled her into national and international fame.   The 35-year-old self-taught herself coding skills through platforms like Harvard Online and SheCodes.     In May 2025, amidst national debate over the controversial Finance Bill 2025, she developed "Civic Email," a simple, one-click platform that enabled thousands of Kenyans to email their objections directly to lawmakers.   This act of digital ingenuity turned an abstract legislative process into a tangible, collective movement and sparked a nationwide conversation about the power of technology in advocacy.   Following the growing popularity of the platform, she was arrested on May 30 and detained over the long Madaraka Day weekend, sparking massive uproar and outrage, with Kenyans calling for her unconditional release.    In October, Njeri was named in the TIME100 Next list, joining a host of influential personalities worldwide.   TIME100 Next is an annual list released by TIME aimed at recognising 100 emerging leaders globally in various fields such as activism, science and technology, arts, sports, film, music, and others.   Speaking after the recognition, Njeri maintained that she would keep going in her activism journey and also thanked those who supported her.

kenya.title: Sofiya Nzau
kenya.summary: Sofiya Nzau Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 6:02 pm Sofiya Nzau, born Sophia Wanjiku in rural Murang'a County, is a groundbreaking singer-songwriter who has become a global sensation by fearlessly infusing traditional Kikuyu language lyrics into contemporary Afro-house and electronic dance music (EDM).   Her journey from working as a street vendor and domestic helper in Thika to becoming a multi-platinum artist is a remarkable testament to her talent and determination.   Discovered after uploading vocal "sound packs" online during the pandemic, she found her signature sound that bridges ancient culture with modern dancefloors, with her powerful, soulful voice making history on the global stage.   In a historic first, she became the first Kenyan and East African artist to perform at Tomorrowland 2025, one of the world's most iconic EDM festivals in Belgium, sharing the stage with superstar DJs like Steve Aoki.   Her global hit " Mwaki ", a collaboration with Brazilian DJ Zerb , continued its monumental run, becoming the most-streamed Kenyan song on Spotify with over 315 million streams by July 2025 and earning platinum certifications in multiple countries.   Further expanding her global footprint, her track "Your Love ( Antdot Remix)" was selected for the official soundtrack of EA Sports FC 26, a major international football video game, marking another significant milestone for Kenyan music on the world stage.   Currently, she has over nine million monthly listeners on Spotify, the largest in East Africa, and has worked with global artists such as Diplo, Steve Aoki, and Avaion .

kenya.title: Tom Gitogo
kenya.summary: Tom Gitogo Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 5:54 pm Tom Gitogo is a highly accomplished financial services executive with over 30 years of experience across Africa and Europe, currently serving as the Group Managing Director and CEO of Britam Holdings Plc, a diversified financial services group operating in seven African countries.   A highly qualified professional, he is a Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW) and holds both an MBA in Strategic Management and a BSc in Civil Engineering from the University of Nairobi.   Gitogo's leadership style is rooted in meticulous planning and a results-oriented approach, which has seen him drive significant growth and profitability in the companies he has led, including previous CEO roles at Sanlam Insurance Kenya and the CIC Insurance Group.   He was recognised as the CEO of the Year (2012) by the Kenya Institute of Management for his outstanding performance at Sanlam.   In March 2025, he was elected the Chairman of the Association of Kenya Insurers (AKI), a role where he is steering the industry through digital transformation, fraud mitigation, and new risks like climate change and AI.   Further acknowledging his leadership, in November 2024, he was voted the second runner-up for the Best People-Focused CEO/MD of the Year at the HR Awards hosted by the Institute of Human Resource Management Kenya.   Britam also earned the prestigious Top Employer Africa 2025 certification in four countries under his leadership, demonstrating his dedication to a purpose-driven and human-centred workplace culture.   Under his leadership, Britam posted a profit before tax of Ksh2.5 billion for the six-month period ended June 30, 2025.   It also recorded an 11 per cent growth in insurance revenue to Ksh19.7 billion, reflecting strong momentum across both the Life and General insurance businesses. Interest and dividend income also grew by 16 per cent to Ksh10.6 billion.

kenya.title: Jepkosgei Chemoiwa
kenya.summary: Jepkosgei Chemoiwa Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 5:34 pm Jepkosgei Chemoiwa is a Kenyan teacher from Baringo County who won the continental award from UNESCO's International Institute for Capacity Building as the best teacher in Africa in September.   A dedicated Mathematics and Physics teacher with over 15 years of experience at Emining Boys High School in Baringo County, Chemoiwa leveraged the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic to pioneer large-scale online learning initiatives that reached thousands of students daily.   Her approach extends beyond traditional teaching; she has been a master trainer in livestreaming and virtual laboratories, introducing digital tools, gamification platforms, and even robotics training to make learning interactive and engaging in underserved regions.   She embodies the spirit of community service, engaging in women's empowerment groups and inspiring excellence in both her students and fellow educators.   Her innovative and dedicated approach has earned her the highest continental recognition. In a landmark achievement in 2025, she was named the African Union Continental Best Teacher by the African Union (AU) in collaboration with UNESCO's International Institute for Capacity Building in Africa (IICBA).   This prestigious award, announced on World Teachers' Day in October, celebrates teachers who demonstrate exceptional commitment to quality education and transformative practices.   Chemoiwa was nominated for the prize by the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

kenya.title: Idd Aziz
kenya.summary: Idd Aziz Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 5:28 pm Idd Aziz is a Kenyan Afro-Fusion and Afro-House musician based in both Kenya and Norway, who gained critical acclaim in 2025.   In July this year, he was named as the most-streamed Kenyan artiste abroad on Spotify in the 2025 Global Impact List.   His hit ‘Time (Mimi)’ featuring the German Artiste Dhali clinched him the top spot, although several other of his tracks made the list, which highlights the top 30 Kenyan songs with the most international streams in the first half of the year.   They include other collaborations like ‘ Mentuliza ’ with Anthony Keyrouz and ‘Penda’ with JimmX .   Additionally, Aziz became the first Kenyan artiste to ever perform at the popular American music festival, Coachella, in April 2025, joining Haitian DJ and producer Francis Mercier on stage to perform their single "Kamili".     Also in the United States, he made more history as the first Kenyan to perform at the world-renowned Burning Man Festival in Nevada in September 2025, sharing the stage with Grammy-winning DJ Black Coffee.

kenya.title: Wandia Gichuru
kenya.summary: Wandia Gichuru Mwanawanjuguna Wed, 12/03/2025 - 5:24 pm Wandia Gichuru is the co-founder and the Chief Executive Officer of Kenya’s Vivo Fashion Group and the e-commerce marketplace ShopZetu.   In January, Gichuru, who is 57 years old, was featured by Forbes magazine in the inaugural ‘50-over-50: Global’ list meant to celebrate women across the globe with significant contributions across various sectors.   Her contribution to the fashion industry gained her a spot, a business that she ventured into in 2011 as just a shop in Nairobi run by two people.   Her impact extends to the e-commerce sector with Shop Zetu , an award-winning marketplace for over 300 local brands.   The government has also honoured her contributions to the nation's economic development, awarding her the Order of the Grand Warrior (OGW) of Kenya in December 2021.   Earlier in her entrepreneurial journey, she was named the Top Woman CEO at the 2018/19 KPMG and Nation Media Top 100 Mid-Size companies awards and received a Distinguished Alumni Award for Leadership & Ingenuity from Citigroup in 2017.   Her brand, Vivo, was also named the Kenyan Fashion Brand of the Year at the Kenya Fashion Awards in both 2016 and 2017.   She told Forbes that she is committed to using her business to create financial opportunities for others, and therefore 100 per cent of Vivo’s designing and manufacturing is done in Kenya

Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty. Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple , Jason and Lucia. entertainment.title: Now get out of that! How can the new James Bond film get around 007’s death in No Time to Die?
entertainment.summary: Was it all a dream? Has Bond been in hiding? Or will Robert Pattinson simply report to HR on his first day? Russell T Davies, David Hare and more give their takes “James Bond will return,” says the closing title on No Time to Die, the most recent James Bond film and the final one to star Daniel Craig. It is just as well: Bond has to all appearances been vaporised by sea-launched missiles, having been infected by nanobots programmed to attack his nearest and dearest at the slightest touch. No one would believe that one of the world’s most successful film series would come to such an abrupt halt, but no doubt a little reassurance helped. Nevertheless, the first order of business for scriptwriter Steven Knight and director Denis Villeneuve will be dealing with it: how to revive and re-energise a character at the heart of the action. Speculation on their best way forward has been rife, and previous examples are not hard to find. Sherlock Holmes was killed off by Arthur Conan Doyle by fighting his arch enemy Professor Moriarty at the Reichenbach Falls in the story The Final Problem, only to resuscitate him a decade later with The Adventure of the Empty House. Superman is apparently killed at the end of Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice, but resurrected in Justice League for the fight against Steppenwolf. Arguably the most enduring pop-culture return is Bobby Ewing’s famous shower scene in the TV show Dallas in 1986, which attempted to ensure continuity by suggesting Ewing’s death was his wife’s dream. And even Ian Fleming toyed with killing off Bond, with a climactic poison scene at the end of his 1957 novel From Russia with Love, and leaving him amnesiac and vulnerable to Soviet attack at the finish of You Only Live Twice, the last Bond novel published in Fleming’s lifetime. entertainment.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
entertainment.summary: Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? From New York via Montana Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children). Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and pathos-drenched, loping forward like an aimless but essential winter morning walk. While Stillwater captures the spirit of 70s singer-songwriter piano ballads, the rest of Eiger’s forthcoming record is rangier and harder to pin down, touching on traditional folk and loose, minimalist prog. It is undoubtedly the best of his projects to date, and is sure to be one of the year’s breakouts, if recent successes by sharp-tongued songwriters such as Cameron Winter and This Is Lorelei are anything to go by. It’s a tale as old as Shrek, which was by no means the first film to subvert fairytale expectations, but it was definitely the most influential, and we’re still feeling its impact 25 years later, for better or worse. What if that villain wasn’t actually the villain after all? What if that love interest shouldn’t have been of interest in the first place?
